chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar from al-Sayyari, raising it, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wishes to apply the lime paste (al-Noura), let him take some of the al-Noura with his finger, smell it, and place it on the tip of his nose, and say:
May Allah send blessings upon Sulayman ibn Dawud, just as He ordered us regarding the al-Noura,
the al-Noura will not burn him.

key_terms.النُّورَةِ: Lime paste used for depilation or skin treatment
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ: Sulayman ibn Dawud (Solomon son of David), a Prophet in Islam

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual method and supplication for applying Noura to prevent burning?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details a specific prophetic tradition for mitigating the burning sensation of *al-Noura* (lime paste), prescribing a ritual of smelling the substance and placing it on the nose while invoking blessings upon Prophet Sulayman. In Shia scholarly tradition, this practice highlights the integration of practical hygiene with spiritual supplication, linking the efficacy of the remedy to the divine authority granted to Sulayman, who is revered in Shia Islam for his mastery over jinn and nature.
